messages.author: 1b2c2ff22fb6659c
messages.subject: Long run time: Error in run_(private$sim_obj, until) : Expecting a single value: [extent=0].
parts:
Created a simulation that runs for short run times and "Error in run_(private$sim_obj) ..." for longer run times.

What is the definition of this error and is there a reason it occurs for longer run times.

Why is it occurring for longer run times:

simulation %>% run(5000)
simmer environment: anonymous | now: 5000 | next: 5052.27699025771


simulation %>% run(7000)
Error in run_(private$sim_obj, until) : Expecting a single value: [extent=0].


I can attempt to recreate the error for a sample simulation if that would be helpful.

Thanks in advance,

messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] Long run time: Error in run_(private$sim_obj, until) : Expecting a single value: [extent=0].
parts:
2018-05-25 20:12 GMT+02:00 <david.j...@gmail.com>:
> Created a simulation that runs for short run times and "Error in
> run_(private$sim_obj) ..." for longer run times.

Note that you will always see that whenever a simulation fails for
whatever reason, simply because the "run" method is *the* method you
call to start the simulation. So for R, it's *the* method that raises
the error, although it's happening in another place: in a trajectory.
But the important bit is the message afterwards (see below).

> What is the definition of this error and is there a reason it occurs for
> longer run times.
>
> Why is it occurring for longer run times:
>
> simulation %>% run(5000)
> simmer environment: anonymous | now: 5000 | next: 5052.27699025771
>
>
> simulation %>% run(7000)
> Error in run_(private$sim_obj, until) : Expecting a single value:
> [extent=0].

This is the error: "Expecting a single value: [extent=0]".
Unfortunately, the runtime is pretty complex (R calling C++ calling R
again), so it's almost impossible to display a meaningful error
telling you where exactly the error is (at the high level).
Fortunately, the message issued by Rcpp usually is meaningful enough
to get some idea of where to look. In this case, "expecting a single
value" means that, at some point, C++ was expecting a single value
from an R function you provided, but didn't get it. What did it get?
Extent=0 means that no value, that is, NULL. Example:

t <- trajectory() %>%
timeout(function() NULL)

simmer() %>%
add_generator("dummy", t, at(0)) %>%
run()
#> Error in run_(private$sim_obj, until) :
#> Expecting a single value: [extent=0].

So review your trajectories and try to find out which function is
returning a NULL value for a longer run time.

> helpful.

> Thanks in advance,

FYI, this patch set [1] enhances error handling, and will be available
in the next release (July). I've replaced the somewhat obscure first
part of the error with some info about the process that raised it, the
simulation time in which it happened and the activity name. For
example, the error above would become:

#> Error: 'dummy0' at 0.00 in 'Timeout':

Still, the error cannot tell you where exacty this is in your R
script, but it provides more clues to look for it.

Iñaki

[1] https://github.com/r-simmer/simmer/pull/148
